messages.author: 6a13cfeca73e7ec3
messages.subject: modSel help
parts:
Unmarked users,

I am using the modSel() function to extract AIC values from 48 permutations of a model fit with pcountOpen.   The function works fine when all the models converge but if something goes wrong and one model does not converge I get the error "Warning message: In sqrt(diag(vcov(x,altNames=TRUE))) : NaNs produced" after the line "msP<-modSel(pfmlist) is submitted.   If I inspect the results from each model, remove the one that did not converge, and then run the modSel() function again it works fine and the AIC values (among other statistics) are printed in a table.  Is there a way to trap this error in the modSel() function so the user doesn't have to manually inspect each model?

I'm running R 2.14.1 with Unmarked v. 0.9-4

Thanks,
Jason

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] modSel help
parts:
Hi Jason,

It looks like you are getting a warning message, not an error. This is supposed to happen, but I'm confused because you should wind up with an object "msP" that has the model selection results. Are you saying that msP is not created at all?

Note also that if your model did not converge, you can't reliably compare it to other models using AIC.

Richard

messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] modSel help
parts:
Marc,

Yes they do, but I don't inspect the model summaries before extracting the
AIC table with modSel. I have the models specified (all permutations with 4
independent variables with the three distributions), run the models and
assign the output to an object (without having the model summary print to
the console), then use modSel to evaluate the AIC values. Based on the AIC
values I will then inspect summaries of the "best" models (change in AIC <
2).

The dataset is from fish community surveys that were conducted at the same
time of year, at the same sites, with the same gear, and protocol for
multiple consecutive years. I am trying to determine what factors (e.g.
area, conductivity, turbidity, and crew leader) affect detectability of the
different fish species we encounter using the pcountOpen model. I believe
that the schooling species violate an assumption of the Dail-Madsen model
and the abundance estimates appear unreasonable. However, abundance and
detection estimates for two of the non-schooling species are in line with
the estimates from depletion surveys I conducted the past 2 years in the
same stream, but different sites, and same electrofishing gear.

Jason
